  <section class="course-intro">
    <p class="course-kicker">School lecture · English · 45 minutes</p>
    <h1>Neutrino Oscillations: from Vacuum to the Earth's Core</h1>
    <p>
      One lecture for students and young scientists of particle physics and
      the Earth sciences, given at the 2026 Fall School on Interdisciplinary
      Neutrino Science in Zhuhai. It starts from an experiment: a neutrino born
      with a positron turns, far from the source, into a muon. Two waves with
      different masses, their beat and its average explain it. Then the vacuum
      and matter as birefringent crystals for neutrinos, solar neutrinos, and
      the lepton mixing matrix from data. Derivations are in tabs; applets
      accompany every step.
    </p>
    <p class="course-author">Dmitry V. Naumov, JINR Dubna · <a href="https://neutrinohit.github.io/">neutrinohit.github.io</a></p>
  </section>

  <section class="course-accordion" aria-label="Lecture and applets">
    <details class="course-row" open>
      <summary>
        <span class="course-row-kind">Lecture</span>
        <span>Neutrino Oscillations in Vacuum and Matter</span>
      </summary>
      <div class="course-row-body">
        <p>
          The problem as an experiment; the quantum chameleon; no flavor field
          has a mass; two waves in and out of phase; the oscillation formula;
          geoneutrinos and atmospheric neutrinos through the Earth. The
          birefringent crystal; the vacuum as a crystal with three axes; the
          refractive index of matter from forward scattering; the ratio A;
          matter turns the axes, the neutrino crystal and the probability in
          matter. Why ν₂ leaves the Sun, with the Borexino data; unitarity and
          the mixing matrix from data; the status of the parameters.
        </p>
        <div class="course-links">
          <a href="en/slides/neutrino_oscillations.html">Open lecture</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </details>

    <details class="course-row">
      <summary>
        <span class="course-row-kind">Applets</span>
        <span>Interactive material inside the lecture</span>
      </summary>
      <div class="course-row-body">
        <p>
          Events counted at a movable detector; survival probability over
          distances from 0.1 to 20 000 km with the geoneutrino spectrum;
          atmospheric neutrinos against the zenith angle; light in a
          birefringent plate; the index matrix and its diagonalization; the
          neutrino crystal; a νe flying out of the Sun; the mixing matrix step
          by step. In the appendix: the adiabatic laboratory, coupled pendulums,
          three-flavor probabilities. All calculations run in the browser.
        </p>
      </div>
    </details>
  </section>
</div>
